::: {.news}
**The course has not started yet.** The diary will be filled lesson by lesson from February 2027. Each lesson is recorded and the recording is linked here, for the students who cannot always attend in presence.

Until then, the slides, blackboard notes, lecture notes and recordings of the [previous edition](https://sites.google.com/diag.uniroma1.it/liberati/home/teaching/2026-systems-and-control-methods-for-cyber-physical-security) cover most of the same topics, in the same order.
:::

## Before the course starts

Three readings that need no prerequisite and show what the course is about:

- [The real story of Stuxnet](https://spectrum.ieee.org/the-real-story-of-stuxnet) (IEEE Spectrum, 2013): how the malware that damaged the centrifuges of an enrichment plant was tracked down, and why the operators saw nothing on their screens.
- [How 30 lines of code blew up a 27-ton generator](https://www.wired.com/story/how-30-lines-of-code-blew-up-27-ton-generator/) (Wired, 2020): the 2007 Aurora experiment, where a protection relay was opened and closed out of phase until the generator destroyed itself.
- [ENTSO-E investigation of the blackout of 28 April 2025 in the Iberian peninsula](https://www.entsoe.eu/publications/blackout/28-april-2025-iberian-blackout/), with the factual report of October 2025 and the final report of March 2026: not an attack, but the clearest recent account of how a disturbance propagates through a power system, which is the physical side of every attack we study.
